title: T(reg) Cells Attenuate Pulmonary Venous Remodeling in PH-LHD via NLRC3 Signaling.
authors: Zhakeer, Gulinigeer; Zeng, Yanxi; E, Guangxi; Maimaitiaili, Nuerbiyemu; Ju, Peinan; Yao, Hongyun; Shi, Yefei; Zhai, Ming; Li, Ke; Zhuang, Jianhui; Cao, Yunshan; Yu, Qing; Peng, Wenhui
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Treg细胞通过NLRC3信号减轻肺静脉重塑，属于免疫与心血管疾病机制研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary venous remodeling is a key pathological feature of pulmonary hypertension associated with left heart disease (PH-LHD). This study aims to investigate the role of regulatory T (T(reg)) cells in this process. METHODS: We used mouse models with transverse aortic constriction and cell depletion of Foxp3-DTR/tdTomato mice to examine T(reg) cells' function around pulmonary veins in PH-LHD in vivo. To confirm the effect of Nlrc3(-/-) T(reg) cells on PH-LHD, we utilized 3 mouse models: Nlrc3 knockout mice, athymic mice, and endothelial cell lineage tracing Cdh5CreERT2(+/)(-)-mT/mG(+/)(-) mice. The interaction proteins and signaling pathways of T(reg) cells during endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition were elucidated by protein docking prediction, coimmunoprecipitation and cocultivation of T(reg) cells with venous endothelial cells. RESULTS: T(reg) cells were abundant around pulmonary veins of transverse aortic constriction-induced PH-LHD and were essential for promoting inflammation resolution and inhibiting pulmonary venous remodeling. Nlrc3 expression was reduced in mice and patients with PH-LHD. NLRC3 (nucleotide-oligomerization domain-like receptor family CARD domain containing 3) deficiency inhibited T(reg) cell proliferation and impaired their immunosuppressive and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition-protective effects. Mechanistically, NLRC3 interacted with TRAM (TRIF-related adaptor molecule) and regulated interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3)/NF-kappaB (nuclear factor-kappaB) p65 signaling in cluster differentiation 4(+) (CD4(+)) T cells. NLRC3-deficient T(reg) cells promoted interleukin (IL)-18 expression through IRF3/NF-kappaB p65 signaling, and thus IL-18 secretion activated endothelial receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling, favoring endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition progression in pulmonary veins and PH-LHD progress. This process was reversible with IL-18 binding protein in vivo. CONCLUSIONS: NLRC3 is crucial for T(reg) cells to prevent pulmonary venous remodeling in PH-LHD, primarily by modulating IL-18 secretion, which inhibits endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and thereby improves disease progression and prognosis.
abstract_zh: 背景：肺静脉重塑是与左心疾病相关的肺动脉高压（PH-LHD）的一个关键病理特征。本研究旨在探讨调节性T（T(reg)）细胞在此过程中的作用。方法：我们使用横向主动脉缩窄小鼠模型和Foxp3-DTR/tdTomato小鼠的细胞耗竭，在体内检查PH-LHD中肺静脉周围T(reg)细胞的功能。为确认Nlrc3(-/-) T(reg)细胞对PH-LHD的影响，我们使用了3种小鼠模型：Nlrc3敲除小鼠、无胸腺小鼠和内皮细胞谱系追踪Cdh5CreERT2(+/)(-)-mT/mG(+/)(-)小鼠。通过蛋白对接预测、共免疫沉淀和T(reg)细胞与静脉内皮细胞共培养，阐明了T(reg)细胞在内皮-间质转化过程中的相互作用蛋白和信号通路。结果：T(reg)细胞在横向主动脉缩窄诱导的PH-LHD肺静脉周围丰富存在，对促进炎症消退和抑制肺静脉重塑至关重要。在PH-LHD小鼠和患者中，Nlrc3表达降低。NLRC3（核苷酸寡聚化结构域样受体家族CARD结构域包含3）缺陷抑制了T(reg)细胞增殖，并损害了其免疫抑制和内-间质转化保护效应。机制上，NLRC3与TRAM（TRIF相关衔接分子）相互作用，并调节簇分化4阳性（CD4(+)）T细胞中的干扰素调节因子3（IRF3）/NF-kappaB（核因子-kappaB）p65信号通路。NLRC3缺陷的T(reg)细胞通过IRF3/NF-kappaB p65信号促进白细胞介素（IL）-18表达，从而IL-18分泌激活内皮受体酪氨酸激酶（RTK）信号，促进肺静脉内-间质转化进展和PH-LHD进程。此过程在体内可通过IL-18结合蛋白逆转。结论：NLRC3对T(reg)细胞在PH-LHD中预防肺静脉重塑至关重要，主要通过调节IL-18分泌，抑制内-间质转化，从而改善疾病进展和预后。
